rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement obliges every link to specialized material to say when to read the file. The file has three such links, and each states its trigger:
- `[CI example](references/ci.md)` appears in "Use the CI example when adding these steps to an existing workflow". The "when setting up or reviewing project CI" sentence before it adds context.
- `[references/distributed-requirements.md](...)` is introduced by "For an obligation that applies separately at each of many sites… read … before drafting it, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`".
- `[references/syntax-details.md](...)` is introduced by "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet… or a requirement lives in a nested chapter, read …".

The mention of `references/fixme.md` is a code span, not a link, and it belongs to another skill. The requirement does not cover it. No violation queries were listed. I found no gap.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
